Pandora. The first woman in Greek mythology, created as punishment for humanity and famous for opening a forbidden jar that released all the world's suffering.

Pandora was created by Zeus himself as a punishment for Prometheus, who had stolen fire for mortals. Zeus commanded Hephaestus, the god of smithcraft, to craft her with irresistible beauty, making her a perfect tool of divine vengeance. Hermes delivered to her a sealed jar containing all the world's miseries, diseases, and hardships.

Pandora married Epimetheus, a Titan brother of Prometheus. Despite warnings from his brother about accepting this gift from the gods, Epimetheus took her as his wife. Pandora opened the jar out of curiosity or temptation, and in that moment, all evils escaped into the world, bringing suffering to all humanity. Only Hope remained trapped in the jar at the bottom, a bittersweet legacy for mankind. Pandora represents the first of womankind and stands as a cautionary figure about the consequences of curiosity and disobedience. She was created by Zeus, the orchestrator of her role as divine punishment. Prometheus, whose theft of fire prompted her creation, bears responsibility for humanity's suffering through her actions. Her husband Epimetheus, whose name means afterthought, showed poor judgment in accepting her. And Hermes delivered the very jar that became the instrument of humanity's suffering.
